classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: the ICE from #120787 only reproduces on build-fail

The patch prevents the move-path gatherer from reaching a `bug!` when error types are encountered during drop elaboration. The concrete pass affected is `ElaborateDrops`, which calls `MoveData::gather_moves` and whose `run_pass` appears in the ICE stack.

processing.reason: The historical change is a compiler-internal error-bailout in `Gatherer::move_path_for`: pre-fix code proceeds to `ProjectionElem::Field` dispatch on a place whose type references `ty::Error` and hits `bug!` (an ICE/abort); the fix adds `if place_ty.references_error() { return MovePathResult::Error; }`. There is no differing defined value semantics to encode as two ordinary Rust functions. The regression input is erroneous Rust source that only has to reach `ElaborateDrops` under `--emit=mir`, and `ty::Error` is a rustc-internal type not expressible as runtime source data. A runnable pair would have to replace the historical abort with an invented sentinel return value; that would not be the actual wrong transformation and would violate source-grounding. Moreover, the historical pre-fix behavior cannot pass Miri because it aborts. Thus no legitimate original/transformed function pair with identical inputs can produce two different defined Miri-observable values for this PR.

analysis.originalLogic: In the MIR move-path builder (`compiler/rustc_mir_dataflow/src/move_paths/builder.rs`), `Gatherer::super_place` computes the current place type with `let place_ty = place_ref.ty(body, tcx).ty;` and then dispatches on the projection `elem`. For `ProjectionElem::Field` it assumes the base place type is a real struct/tuple/enum type and contains an assertion that is reached when the type is instead an error type: `When Place contains ProjectionElem::Field it's type shouldn't be {type error}`. `ElaborateDrops` invokes `MoveData::gather_moves`, so any error type flowing into a field projection during drop elaboration reaches that `bug!`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Before the fix, the gatherer did not inspect the computed place type for error types; it unconditionally continued matching the projection element. Consequently a `ProjectionElem::Field` projection on a place whose type references a type error reached the `bug!`/ICE in `gather_move` instead of gracefully returning an error result. The corrected behavior is the early guard `if place_ty.references_error() { return MovePathResult::Error; }`, which bails out of move-path gathering for the error-containing place before element dispatch.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source that already contains type errors but still proceeds far enough to run drop elaboration / MIR analysis, especially with `--emit=mir`. Convergence test shape: a struct with nontrivial drop glue (`struct Foo { field: String }`), a `type Tait = impl Sized;` alias under `#![feature(type_alias_impl_trait)]`, a function taking a `Tait` parameter and destructuring it (`let Foo { field } = beverage;`), plus an unrelated type error in `main` (`Ok(())` where the default return type is `()`), producing E0308 while drop elaboration runs for the enclosing/closure body. The issue reproducer uses `pub async fn ice_cold(beverage: Tait)` and comments that the field `/// This type must have nontrivial drop glue` and `/// Must destructure at least one field of `Foo``.
analysis.summary: Bug-fix PR for an ICE in drop elaboration when a place whose type references a type error is traversed with a `ProjectionElem::Field`. The fix makes the move-path gatherer return `MovePathResult::Error` when `place_ty.references_error()`, before the projection-element dispatch that otherwise hits `When Place contains ProjectionElem::Field it's type shouldn't be {type error}`. Reusable knowledge: error types can legitimately reach MIR drop elaboration, so move-path construction must treat them as an error bail-out rather than asserting well-formedness. The regression test is a UI test compiled with `--emit=mir`.
analysis.trigger: Running `ElaborateDrops` (via `mir_drops_elaborated_and_const_checked`) on MIR where a place used in a field projection has a type that references a type error, e.g. destructuring a struct out of a TAIT/opaque-typed value in a crate that also has a type error.
preconditions: The crate contains a type error but compilation still reaches MIR drop elaboration (not stopped at an earlier check-fail stage).
A place whose type references an error type appears as the base of a `ProjectionElem::Field` during move-path gathering.
The destructured type has nontrivial drop glue so drop elaboration/gathering is exercised.
Using `type_alias_impl_trait` with `type Tait = impl Sized;` provides the error-referencing place type in the regression test.
Test must use `--emit=mir` because the ICE does not reproduce under build-fail.
pitfalls: Do not mark the regression test build-fail: the added test comment says `can't use build-fail, because this also fails check-fail, but the ICE from #120787 only reproduces on build-fail.` and instead uses `// compile-flags: --emit=mir`.
Do not conflate this with a general borrowck or drop-scheduling change; the concrete failure is move-path gathering during `ElaborateDrops` hitting a `bug!` on an error-typed place.
The error type may be indirect: `place_ty.references_error()` (via `TypeVisitableExt`) is broader than checking only the top-level type, so a guard on exact type equality would miss nested errors.
The test's only expected diagnostic is E0308 from `main`; the ICE must be gone rather than merely replaced by another error.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test `tests/ui/drop/drop_elaboration_with_errors.rs` with `#![feature(type_alias_impl_trait)]`, `struct Foo { field: String }`, `type Tait = impl Sized;`, a function `fn ice_cold(beverage: Tait)` doing `let Foo { field } = beverage; _ = field;`, and `fn main() { Ok(()) //~ ERROR mismatched types }`. Compile it with `// compile-flags: --emit=mir` so drop elaboration runs; assert the stderr contains only the E0308 mismatched-types diagnostic (expected `()`, found `Result<(), _>`) and no ICE. For a two-program differential check, vary only the guard/transformation (error-type bail-out vs. proceeding into the field-projection dispatch) while keeping the same source.
